answer: Cap rewards per behavioural cluster, not per address. A sybil farm runs one model behind many keys, so each epoch its answers and grades rise as a ridge of near-identical phrasing and timing. Peers embed every answer; addresses that keep landing in the same tight cluster share one reward slot. Like water seeping through karst, the shared operator leaks through, and a single ripple of copied style collapses fifty keys into one payout, so extra keys add cost but no income.
